BiblicalUsage: Cheyva is the Aramaic word for a beast, an animal, and Daniel uses it in the visions of the kingdoms. The beasts of the field are given into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, the great tree shelters the beasts beneath it, and the king himself is told he will dwell with the beasts of the field until he knows that the Most High rules.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the beast in Daniel shows how low a proud king can fall, and how high God lifts those who humble themselves. I hold that every kingdom that forgets God becomes a beast, and only His kingdom endures.
RelatedEvents: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Image; Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
